units.text: The Welcome and First Lodging in Madinah
How did the people of Madinah welcome the Prophet ﷺ before he stayed in Abu Ayyub’s house, and how do Ibn Ishaq’s and Aflah’s accounts differ about the floors?

How did Madinah welcome the Messenger of God ﷺ, and how did Abu Ayyub’s house become his first home there? Al-Bara’ relates the people’s joy; Anas recalls first hearing news of his arrival and then seeing the welcome. The repeated invitations to stay, with the names of those who offered them, come from Ibn Ishaq’s Sira, before Anas’s hadith recounts the party’s arrival at Abu Ayyub’s courtyard.

From Abu Ayyub’s courtyard to his house, the account of hospitality expands: in Ibn Ishaq’s report Abu Ayyub describes the Prophet ﷺ staying on the lower floor, the household’s care when the water jar broke, and the supper they prepared for him.
When news of the arrival spread

Work preceded the wait for his arrival: al-Bara’ mentions Mus’ab ibn Umayr and Ibn Umm Maktum teaching people to recite, then names those who came after them. He says he had never seen the people of Madinah rejoice over anything as they did over the Messenger of God ﷺ; news of the arrival spread even among the slave girls.

Anas recalls running with the boys whenever they heard that Muhammad ﷺ had arrived, only to find that the newcomer was not him. When the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr did come, he recalls about five hundred of the Ansar welcoming them, and the people of Madinah coming out, while young women looked down from the rooftops and asked which of the arrivals was the Prophet ﷺ.

In another report from Anas, he says he had never seen a day more beautiful or radiant than the day the Prophet ﷺ entered; in the longer report he says that, for him, the day of his arrival and the day of his death were unlike other days.
Invitations along the road to the lodging

As the account moves from Quba to Madinah, Ibn Hajar quotes Ibn Ishaq and Ibn A’idh on the Prophet’s ﷺ departure on Friday and his reaching the Friday prayer among Banu Salim ibn Awf, where Ibn Ishaq’s report begins its account of the local people offering him lodging.

In Ibn Ishaq’s account, Itban ibn Malik and Abbas ibn Ubada, together with men of Banu Salim, invite him to stay with them, citing their numbers, equipment, and ability to protect him. Similar offers then come from men of Banu Bayada, Banu Saida, Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, and Banu Adi ibn al-Najjar.

In Ibn Ishaq’s report, the Prophet ﷺ responds to each offer of lodging by asking the people to let his she-camel go her way, saying that she is under orders. They clear her path in the account, and she goes on to another invitation.
To Abu Ayyub’s courtyard

In al-Bukhari’s hadith, Anas describes the Prophet ﷺ riding his mount with Abu Bakr behind him and a gathering of Banu al-Najjar around him, until he reaches Abu Ayyub’s courtyard. From there Anas’s account moves on to prayer and the matter of the mosque and its construction.

The Prophet ﷺ stayed in Abu Ayyub’s house, Ibn Ishaq says, until the mosque and the dwellings were built, and then moved into his dwellings. Abu Ayyub relates some of what took place in the house between those two points.
In the host’s house

In Ibn Ishaq’s report Abu Ayyub describes the Prophet ﷺ staying on the lower floor of the house while he and Umm Ayyub stayed upstairs. He asks for the Prophet ﷺ to stay above them, but the Prophet replies: “Abu Ayyub, it is more convenient for us and for those who visit us to be on the lower floor of the house.” According to the rest of this report, Abu Ayyub and Umm Ayyub remain upstairs.

In the continuation of his report in Ibn Ishaq, Abu Ayyub recounts that a jar of water broke upstairs. He and Umm Ayyub began soaking up the water with a cloth they owned, for fear that some might drip onto the Prophet ﷺ and harm him.

In the same report, Abu Ayyub says that he and Umm Ayyub used to prepare the Prophet’s ﷺ supper and, when he sent back the remainder, they would seek out the place his hand had touched, hoping for blessing. They sent him supper containing onion or garlic, but Abu Ayyub found no trace of his hand in it. When he asked, the Prophet ﷺ said he had smelled that plant and that he held intimate discourse [with God]; he told the household they could eat it.
Between the account of arrival and the account of residence

Al-Bara’ describes the people’s joy after naming those who arrived before the Prophet ﷺ to teach them recitation; Anas’s report in al-Bayhaqi, by contrast, speaks of waiting with the boys and of the Ansar’s welcome. In his longer report Anas mentions about five hundred Ansar welcoming the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr; his shorter report describes the day of arrival without giving a day of the month.

Ibn Hajar attributes the account of the Friday departure to Ibn Ishaq and Ibn A’idh and quotes al-Hakim on the she-camel kneeling at Abu Ayyub’s door; Anas’s hadith in al-Bukhari, however, says they reached Abu Ayyub’s courtyard. Ibn Ishaq says the Prophet ﷺ stayed in Quba on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, and reports Banu Amr ibn Awf’s claim that he stayed among them longer than that.
The Two Floors and the Food in Abu Ayyub’s House

Ibn Ishaq’s report leaves Abu Ayyub and Umm Ayyub upstairs when it relates the broken jar. In the account through Aflah from Abu Ayyub in Muslim, the people upstairs moved to one side because they disliked walking above the Prophet ﷺ; the account ends with the Prophet ﷺ moving upstairs and Abu Ayyub downstairs.

Ibn Ishaq’s report says onion or garlic, expressing uncertainty, and quotes the Prophet’s ﷺ reply about the smell of the plant and his private communication. In Muslim’s account through Simak, garlic is named without this uncertainty, and the dislike is explained by its smell, not by a prohibition of the food. In the account through Aflah in Muslim, his ﷺ answer is: “No, but I dislike it.” Yahya ibn Sa’id’s corroborating report from Shu’ba gives the chain without repeating the text.

“I used to run with the boys when they said, ‘Muhammad has come!’ I would run and see nothing. Then they would say, ‘Muhammad has come!’ and I would run and see nothing, until the Prophet ﷺ and his companion Abu Bakr arrived. We lay concealed by [33] one of the walls of Madinah, then sent a man from the desert to notify the Ansar of their arrival. About five hundred of the Ansar came to meet the two, until they reached them. The Ansar said, ‘Go forward, safe and obeyed.’ The Messenger of God ﷺ and his companion approached in their midst. The people of Madinah came out, so that even the young women [34] on the rooftops looked out at him, saying, ‘Which one is he? Which one is he?’ We saw no sight like it that day.” Anas said: “I saw the day he came to us and the day he died, and I have seen no two days like those.” [35]
